<!--
Full reference for the Simplified Technical English house style.
CLAUDE.md carries the short version; this file carries the complete rules and word list.
-->

# Simplified Technical English

This is our house style, adapted from ASD-STE100 for software work. It is an adaptation, not
the specification. ASD-STE100 comes from the AeroSpace and Defence Industries Association of
Europe, or ASD. The ASD specification is copyrighted, so this file contains no text from it
and no part of its approved-word dictionary. Download the real specification from
asd-ste100.org if you need the source.

CLAUDE.md carries the short version, and the short version is what runs by default. Read this
file when you rewrite a document. Read it also when you need the complete word list, or when
a rule in CLAUDE.md is unclear.

## Why we do this

Short, plain, consistent sentences are faster to read and harder to misread. Every reader
gets the same meaning from the same words. This matters most for people who read under load:
on call, mid-incident, or three weeks after they last saw the code.

## Scope

The rules apply to:

1. Chat responses.
2. Markdown documents, architecture decision records, plans, and READMEs.
3. Code comments and docstrings.
4. Commit messages, merge request descriptions, and tickets.

## Exemptions

These are outside the rules. Do not rewrite them.

1. **Technical Names.** Nouns that name a real thing: `useEffect`, `Temporal`, `FHIR`,
   `DynamoDB`, `pnpm`, a file path, a branch name, an error code.
2. **Technical Verbs.** Verbs that name a real operation: `commit`, `rebase`, `merge`,
   `deploy`, `mock`, `lint`, `serialize`.
3. **Code.** Identifiers, snippets, and command lines.
4. **Quoted output.** Tool output, logs, and error text stay verbatim.
5. **Jokes and asides.** Banter is exempt. The rules govern technical explanation,
   instructions, and written artifacts. See the humor rule in CLAUDE.md.

An exempt word does not make the sentence around it exempt. Write a plain sentence with the
technical name inside it.

## Rules

### Words

1. Use the plainest word that carries the meaning. See the word list below.
2. Give one word one meaning. Pick a word for a concept and use only that word for it.
3. Give one meaning one word. Do not switch between synonyms for variety.
4. Do not use a noun as a verb, or a verb as a noun. Write "we changed the config", not
   "we actioned the change". Write "the build failed", not "there was a build failure".
5. Spell out an abbreviation the first time you use it, unless it is a Technical Name.
6. Do not use idiom, slang, or metaphor in technical text. "The test is flaky" is fine
   because it is our standard term. "The test is a house of cards" is not.

### Verbs

7. Use the active voice. Write "the migration dropped the column", not "the column was
   dropped by the migration".
8. Use the present tense for how things are. Use the past tense only for what happened.
9. Do not use an `-ing` form as a verb or as a noun. Write "this breaks the build", not
   "this is breaking the build". Write "to parse the file", not "parsing the file".
10. Use an `-ing` or `-ed` form as a plain adjective: "the running process", "the failed
    job".
11. Use the imperative for instructions. Write "run the tests", not "you should run the
    tests" and not "the tests should be run".

### Sentences

12. Keep an instruction to 20 words or fewer.
13. Keep a statement to 25 words or fewer.
14. Write one instruction per sentence. Split "open the file and change line 40" into two
    sentences, or into two numbered steps.
15. Write one topic per sentence.
16. Keep articles. Write "run the script", not "run script".
17. Do not stack more than three nouns. Rewrite "user auth token refresh failure" as "the
    refresh of the user auth token failed".

### Paragraphs

18. Keep a paragraph to six sentences or fewer.
19. Write one topic per paragraph. Start with the topic.
20. Use a numbered list for a sequence. Use a bulleted list for a set.
21. Keep list items parallel. If item 1 starts with a verb, every item starts with a verb.

### Warnings

22. Put the warning before the step it applies to, never after.
23. Write a warning as a plain command: "Stop the server before you run this."
24. Say what happens if the reader ignores it.

### Punctuation

25. Use a hyphen only to join a compound adjective before a noun: "read-only file".
26. Do not use a slash for "or". Write "the branch or the tag", not "the branch/tag".
27. Do not use parentheses for a second thought. Write a second sentence.

## Message structure

These are ours, not ASD's. They govern the shape of a message, not the language in it.

28. Make the first line the next action, not context and not a plan.
29. Number multi-step work. One bounded action per step.
30. Restate where we are every turn: which step, how many remain.
31. Give time estimates in concrete units. "About 15 minutes", not "some work".
32. Say what now works, in concrete terms.
33. Keep a list to five items. Past the fifth item, split the list into "now" and "later".
34. Cut the preamble, the recap, and the closing pleasantries. Start with the answer. Stop
    when the answer is done.
35. State an error as cause and fix. No "uh oh" and no "there seems to be a problem".

## When to relax the rules

1. The reader asks you to explain a topic step by step. Run as long as the topic needs. The
   language rules still hold.
2. A destructive action is next. Confirm first. Safety is more important than brevity.
3. Three turns of "still broken". Stop the edits to the code. Name the assumption that may be
   wrong. Ask one diagnostic question.
4. The request is truly ambiguous. Ask one short question.

Use the word on the right.

## Examples

Before: "In order to ensure the migration completes successfully, it is necessary to
initially verify that a sufficient number of connections are currently available, and
subsequently the script should be executed by the operator."

After: "First, check that enough connections are free. Then run the script."

Before: "We're currently leveraging the existing user auth token refresh failure handler to
facilitate retries."

After: "The handler for a failed refresh of the user auth token now retries."

Before: "Parsing the response is breaking because the schema was modified by the last
deploy."

After: "The last deploy changed the schema. The parse of the response now fails."
# 4thandgoal

This repo holds three apps. The site and the pipeline each have a CLAUDE.md with its own commands and rules. Read the one for the app you change.

- [Site](apps/site/README.md) in `apps/site/` is the Next.js site. Its build copies `clients/<slug>/published/` of one client into `public/` and renders each `page.json` and its images.
- [Pipeline](apps/pipeline/README.md) in `apps/pipeline/` is the Python pipeline. It builds each week and publishes it into `clients/<slug>/published/`.
- [API](apps/api/README.md) in `apps/api/` serves the trade analyzer and deploys to Fly. Its product code imports no pipeline code. Run `make help` in it.

For module ownership, follow root instructions → app README → owner README → module and test.
Choose the responsibility in the app map, then follow its owner links.

The root holds one uv workspace and one pnpm workspace, each with one lock file: `uv.lock` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
Run `uv sync --all-packages` and `pnpm install` at the root. A member runs with `uv run --exact --package <name>`.

## Style

Write all output in Simplified Technical English. Rules: `~/.claude/rules/communication/simplified-technical-english.md`. Active voice, present tense, one instruction per sentence, 20 words or fewer, no `-ing` as a verb, plain words. Code, technical names, and quoted output are exempt.

## Records

- `GLOSSARY.md` holds the terms of both apps, one section per app, and the workflow terms. Each term has one meaning.
- `docs/adr/` holds one ADR series for both apps. `docs/adr/README.md` maps each old app number to its new number.

## The flow

ADRs 0018 to 0021 and ADR 0026 set the flow. ADR 0026 supersedes ADR 0020. The spec `.scratch/one/` builds it, so its own tickets still merge to `main` as before.

1. `main` is the record branch. No agent commits on `main` or pushes to `main` (ADR 0019).
2. A spec branch is named `<slug>` and starts from `main`.
3. A ticket branch is named `<slug>-<NN>`. It is local, starts from the spec branch, and has its own worktree.
4. A ticket merges into its spec branch with `git merge --no-edit`, after the check passes.
5. One pull request goes from the spec branch to `main`, as a squash merge.
6. An agent records the evidence of each acceptance test `AT-<n>`. The agent gives no test verdict.
7. A fresh subagent, the Judge, gives PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED for each test in `VERDICTS.md`. A check blocks the merge until each test has PASS. A FAIL from Brian in a PR comment overrides the Judge (ADR 0026).

The weekly `publish` is the one exception. It may push to `main`, and it may stage only `clients/<slug>/published/<season>/`, `clients/<slug>/data/<season>/`, and `clients/<slug>/build/<season>/`.

The repo plugin `4ag` takes an idea to a merged spec. Run its skills in this order. Brian approves the output of each of steps 2 to 4.

1. `4ag:plan <outcome statement>` writes the map and the decision tickets. `4ag:plan <feature>` clears one decision ticket per session.
2. `4ag:to-spec <feature>` writes `PRD.md`.
3. `4ag:to-acceptance <feature>` writes `ACCEPTANCE.md`.
4. `4ag:to-tickets <feature>` writes the tickets and the `state.md` row.
5. `4ag:implement <feature>` builds each ticket on its ticket branch, merges it into the spec branch, records the evidence in `EVIDENCE.md`, has the Judge write `VERDICTS.md`, and opens one PR to `main`.
6. Brian posts no comment unless he gives a FAIL. `4ag:review <PR number>` does one round of feedback per run. The check `verdict` passes when each test has PASS from the Judge and no FAIL from Brian, and Brian merges.

## Tracker

The tracker is local markdown, because the notes name league managers and the repo is public (ADR 0021).

- The tracker is `.scratch/<feature>/` at the root, for both apps. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
- A feature that both old trackers held keeps a `site/` and a `pipeline/` subfolder, each with its own PRD and `issues/`.
- A new feature has an optional `MAP.md`, `decisions/`, `PRD.md`, `ACCEPTANCE.md`, and `issues/`. Old features keep their shape.

## Where the work sits

`docs/agents/state.md` lists each open feature, its next ticket, and its blocker. An agent new to the repo reads it
after this file, then reads one ticket in the tracker.

## Commits

The prek hook runs `pnpm check:fast` of the site, then `make check-fast` of the pipeline and of the API, before each commit.
Never commit with `--no-verify`.
# Cornerstone Weekly

This repo builds the weekly report site for the Cornerstone fantasy football league. The
data comes from Sleeper. The public site of CPC is at https://cpc.4thandgoal.app/

## Module map

- Build and publish orchestration: the [cornerstone owner](src/cornerstone/README.md) joins the weekly stages and controls publish commits.
- Domain packages: the [week owner](../../packages/week/README.md) owns weekly facts and page data. Its [sheet owner](../../packages/week/python/src/week/sheet/README.md) owns roster projections. Packages hold domain rules; the app joins their outputs.

## Commands

Each command that reads a league names its client with `--client <slug>`, such as `--client cpc`. A command with no
slug stops with a plain message. The client folder `clients/<slug>/` at the repo root holds `client.toml` and `data/`.

- `cornerstone build` builds the data of a week: `page.json` and the images.
- `cornerstone publish` copies the week folder to `clients/<slug>/published/` of this repo and pushes it.
- `cornerstone rewrite --chapter <key>` rewrites one chapter.
- `cornerstone page-json` writes `page.json` for a saved week.
- `cornerstone settings` prints the League settings of a season and each size that derives from them.
- `cornerstone check-client <folder>` checks the `client.toml` of a client folder and the exported schema.

## Setup

Run `prek install` one time per clone. The hook then runs `make check-fast` before each commit.
Each worktree reads its own branch's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

## Makefile

The `Makefile` holds the common tasks. Run `make help` to list them. A weekly run uses three targets:

1. `make build CLIENT=cpc WEEK=<W>` builds the week.
2. `make publish CLIENT=cpc WEEK=<W>` copies the week to `clients/cpc/published/` and pushes it.
3. `make push` pushes `main`. It stops if the branch is not `main` or the tree is not clean.

## Tuesday runbook

1. At 8:00 the launchd job builds the week and shows a notification. The job is `com.briankwon.cornerstone-weekly`. Its log is `~/Library/Logs/cornerstone-weekly/build.log`.
2. Read the week data, or the page after the site deploys.
3. Run `cornerstone rewrite --client cpc --chapter <key>` for each chapter that needs a fix.
4. Run `cornerstone publish --client cpc`.
5. Share the home page link: https://cpc.4thandgoal.app/

## Page data for the site

The build writes JSON and images only. It writes no HTML. The site repo renders the pages from
the JSON, including the home page.

The build writes `clients/<slug>/build/<season>/week-NN/page.json` with the images beside it.
Each client has its own build folder, so the build of one client never overwrites the files of another. The file holds the
render context and a `schema_version` key. The image paths in it are relative to the week folder.
The default avatar and headshot paths point to `images/` under `apps/site/public/`, and the site repo serves
those files.

`cornerstone publish` copies the whole week folder to `clients/<slug>/published/<season>/week-NN/` in the
repo. It copies no `images/` folder and writes no `index.html`. The site repo reads `summary` from
each `page.json` to list the weeks on the home page.

To write the file for a saved week, run `cornerstone page-json --client <slug> --season <S> --week <W>`. The
command reads the saved facts and blurbs. It makes no writer call and no network call.

Bump `PAGE_SCHEMA_VERSION` in `src/cornerstone/render.py` when a key changes meaning or leaves.
A new key does not need a bump.

Schema version 2 removed the `asset_version` and `root` keys. Only the retired templates read them.

# Cornerstone Weekly

## Purpose

This tool builds a weekly report page for the Cornerstone fantasy football league. It reads
league data from Sleeper. It writes the chapters of the report and writes the page data. The site in `apps/site` renders the pages.
The root CLAUDE.md holds the style, the flow, and the tracker. `GLOSSARY.md` names the chapter of prose a "Prose block".

For module ownership, start with the [app map](README.md). Follow its owner README links to the module and test.

## Commands

Run these in `apps/pipeline/`. Run `make help` for the full list.

- Install: `make install`. The root `uv.lock` holds the locked versions of the whole uv workspace.
- Check: `make check`. The hook runs `make check-fast`.
- Build a week: `make build CLIENT=cpc WEEK=<W>`. Each league target needs the client slug.
- Publish a week: `make publish CLIENT=cpc WEEK=<W>`. It commits `clients/<slug>/build/<season>/`, `clients/<slug>/data/<season>/`, and `clients/<slug>/published/<season>/`, then pushes `main`.
- Local API on port 8080: `make -C ../api api`. The API is its own app in `apps/api/`.

## Pipeline

1. Fetch the raw league data from Sleeper.
2. Save the raw data under `clients/<slug>/data/` and cache the shared NFL data under `data/nfl/cache/`, both at the repo root.
3. Compute the stats for each chapter.
4. Write the chapter text with the Anthropic API.
5. Write `page.json` and the images into the build folder `clients/<slug>/build/`.
6. Publish the week folder to `clients/<slug>/published/` of this repo.

## Where the work sits

`docs/agents/state.md` at the repo root lists each open feature of both apps, its next ticket, and its hold. Read it, then the
ticket in the root tracker under `.scratch/`.

## Publish rule

Nothing publishes without `cornerstone publish`. No other command or script pushes the site.

## Tests

- Run `uv run pytest` for the default suite. It skips tests marked `live`.
- A test marked `live` calls a real external API. Run it on purpose with `uv run pytest -m live`.
- Run `make check` before a merge. The prek hook runs `make check-fast` on each commit.
- Name a rule test `tests/test_rule_<topic>.py`. `make rules` finds each one with no edit.

## House style

Prose follows Simplified Technical English. The rules are in
`~/.claude/rules/communication/simplified-technical-english.md`.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Local markdown under `.scratch/<feature>/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

The five default names, unchanged. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context: `GLOSSARY.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root, shared with the site. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.
# cornerstone

## Knows

- The weekly build: fetch from the provider, parse, build the fact sheet, write, verify, render, and publish. [publish.py](publish.py) owns `run_publish` and limits commits to the client season paths. [test_rule_publish.py](../../tests/test_rule_publish.py) checks stray files and other seasons.
- The `advisor-eval` command of the CLI. The `analyzer` package holds the fact sheet, the Advisor, and the Finder.
- The build of each week and the season files. The `rankings`, `managers`, and `waiver` packages hold their own rules.
- The build and the publish of the midseason report: `midseason` runs the sim through `season_sim.py`, reads the pairs left through `season_schedule.py`, and writes the draft and the review file, and `midseason-publish` checks each blurb again and commits `midseason.json` and `sim.json`.
- The six layers: model, provider, load, facts, write, output. A module imports only from its own layer or a lower one.
- The shared kernel is the league package in `packages/league/`. Every outside service enters through it.
- The fact tokens, the writer, the verifier, and the default voice are the facts package in `packages/facts/`.
- `LAYER_OF` in `tests/test_layers.py` gives the layer of each module. `docs/adr/0010-six-layers-import-downward-only.md` gives the reason. The terms are in `GLOSSARY.md`.

## Ports

- `Writer` in `league/claude_port.py`: the one Claude call. `ClaudeWriter` in `facts/writer.py` implements it. Its key is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `Jev` in `league/jev_port.py`: the one TypeSafe Jev request. `TypeSafeJev` in `league/jev.py` implements it. Its key is `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.
- The `Provider` port is in `league/provider/`. `tests/fakes.py` holds the one fake of each port: `FixtureProvider`, `FakeWriter`, and `FakeJev`.

## Does not do

- It never imports `cornerstone_api`. The [API owner](../../../api/src/cornerstone_api/README.md) serves the trade analyzer over HTTP.
- It builds no HTML. The site repo builds the HTML from each published file.
- No module reads a global client. The CLI or the API entry builds the Client once with `load_client` and passes it down.

    57	    # checkout. A fixed path to a second checkout breaks in a worktree and on any other machine.
    58	    result = subprocess.run(
    59	        ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd=repo, check=False, capture_output=True, text=True
    60	    )
    61	    if result.returncode != 0:
    62	        raise PublishError(f"{repo} is not in a git checkout: {result.stderr.strip()}")

    67	        repo: Path, season: int, week: int, slug: str, folder: Path, site_repo: Path | None = None,
    68	        push: bool = True) -> str:
    69	    """Publish one week of the client `slug`. `folder` is the client folder, which holds its build folder and its
    70	    data. The site repo is the root of the pipeline's checkout, unless a test names another."""
    71	    build = build_dir(folder)
    72	    data = folder / "data"
    73	    page = site_week_dir(build, season, week) / "page.json"
    74	    if not page.exists():
    75	        raise PublishError(f"{page} does not exist. Build the week first.")
    76	    if site_repo is None:
    77	        site_repo = _repo_root(repo)
    78	    # Check the site repo before the first commit, so a bad path leaves no half-done publish.
    79	    if not (site_repo / ".git").exists():
    80	        raise PublishError(f"{site_repo} is not a git checkout.")
    81	
    82	    # Why: ADR 0019 lets the publish stage only the season folders of the client. The build folder holds the season
    83	    # files that the next build reads, and the API image seeds from the data folder, so both go into the report commit.
    84	    # A season folder with no files yet has nothing to stage.
    85	    report = [str(path) for path in (season_dir(build, season), season_dir(data, season)) if path.exists()]
    86	    _git(folder, "add", "--", *report)
    87	    _commit_if_staged(folder, f"Week {week} report", *report)
    88	
    89	    # Copy only this week: its page.json, avatars, and headshots. A built but unpublished week must
    90	    # stay off the public site. The site is a Next.js app. It renders the pages and the home
    91	    # page from these folders.
    92	    # Why: each client keeps its data in its own folder, and the site build copies only that client's published data.
    93	    public_dir = site_repo / "clients" / slug / "published"
    94	    week_path = Path(str(season)) / week_label(week)
    95	    shutil.copytree(
    96	        build / week_path, public_dir / week_path, dirs_exist_ok=True
    97	    )

    99	    rankings = season_dir(build, season) / "rankings.json"
   100	    if rankings.exists():

   102	    else:
   103	        log.warning("%s missing: the publish goes out without rankings.json", rankings)

   105	    managers = season_dir(build, season) / "managers.json"

   125	def midseason_page_url(slug: str, season: int) -> str:

   130	def run_midseason_publish(
   131	        repo: Path, season: int, week: int, call: ClaudeCall, *, client: Client, site_repo: Path | None = None,
   132	        push: bool = True) -> str:
   133	    """Publish the draft of the midseason report of `week`. The verifier checks each blurb of the draft again, so an
   134	    edit cannot add an uncited number or claim. On a failure, nothing is copied and nothing is committed.
   135	
   136	    Why: the publish rule of ADR 0019 lets a publish stage only the season folders of the client. This publish stages
   137	    only its two files in the published season folder. It then pushes, as the weekly publish does, so the report goes
   138	    live with no second step.
   139	    """
   140	    season_build = season_dir(build_dir(client.folder), season)
   141	    missing = [name for name in MIDSEASON_FILES if not (season_build / name).exists()]
   142	    if missing:
   143	        raise PublishError(f"{season_build} has no {' and no '.join(missing)}. Build the report first.")
   144	    report = read_midseason(season_build)
   145	    if report.week != week:
   146	        raise PublishError(f"The draft is the report of week {report.week}, not week {week}. "
   147	                           f"Run make midseason CLIENT={client.slug} WEEK={week} first.")
   148	    if site_repo is None:
   149	        site_repo = _repo_root(repo)
   150	    if not (site_repo / ".git").exists():
   151	        raise PublishError(f"{site_repo} is not a git checkout.")
   152	    failures = recheck_prose(report_blurbs(report), read_draft_facts(season_build), call,
   153	                             prompts_dir=client.voice_dir)
   154	    if failures:
   155	        refusal = "Nothing is published. Fix each blurb in the draft, then run the publish again."
   156	        raise PublishError("\n".join([*failures, refusal]))

   158	    public_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    14	ALLOWED = ("clients/cpc/published/2026/", "clients/cpc/data/2026/", "clients/cpc/build/2026/")

    30	    """Each path of the commit outside the season folders of the client. The line is 1, because a path has no line."""
    31	    return [Offense(

    36	        rule=RULE,

    44	    commits = _git(root, "rev-list", "HEAD").split()

    64	    _git(root, "init", "-b", "main")

    66	    _git(root, "config", "user.name", "Test")
